messages:
Alex: Quick sync — we need a single mapping doc that ties pricing plans -> quota rules for enforcement and the console. Free / Pro / Enterprise. Also how bursts work (per-key vs per-org) and what telemetry we expose.
Priya: +1. I sketched something small, will paste.
Priya: Proposal summary: Free = soft limits with short cooldowns; Pro = firm token quotas + small burst; Enterprise = contracted quotas, larger burst window + rate-smoothing.
Ben: Important callout: per-org quotas for enterprise customers (so shared pool) but per-key for free/pro to avoid noisy neighbors.
Maya: Curious about burst semantics — do we want token-bucket style (instant burst) or a leaky-bucket smoothing over 60s?
Priya: I prefer token-bucket for responsiveness, with a secondary leaky window to avoid sustained overage. Example config: ```json
{
  "plan": "pro",
  "monthly_tokens": 5000000,
  "burst_capacity": 50000,
  "burst_window_sec": 60,
  "enforcement_mode": "hard"
}
```
Ben: That looks fine. Two operational Qs: 1) How do we charge for burst overage? 2) How to signal throttled requests in the API/console?
Alex: For billing, bursts count against monthly tokens for pro/free. Enterprise can have separate negotiated overage or soft-credit controls. For signaling: 429 + body with fields {"quota_remaining","burst_available","reset_in"}. Make the console surface a per-key / per-org graph + alerts.
Maya: Telemetry wise we need: metric names and labels. Minimal set: quota.used{plan,org,key}, quota.burst_used{plan,org,key}, quota.enforcement.action{deny,throttle,allow}, quota.reset.seconds. Also events for "quota.near_limit".
Priya: Agree. Also we should emit diagnostic headers for internal calls: `X-Quota-Remaining`, `X-Quota-Burst` so SDKs can show user-friendly UX.
Ben: How about enforcement ordering? If per-key exhausted but org pool has tokens, do we allow fallback to org pool?
Alex: Yes — fallback allowed only for Enterprise when entitlement includes shared-pool. For free/pro no fallback. Document an explicit policy matrix.
Priya: UX on console: show both key-level and org-level lines, with clear color-coding and a toggle to view historic burst events. Also add a quick action to request a quota bump (links to support flow).
Maya: Ops concern: we need a cheap fast-path check for admission control (in edge proxy) and an authoritative check async in the quota service to reconcile. Edge should cache small token buckets per key for <1s to avoid rps hit.
ops-sre: +1 — we'll add an admission LRU cache and circuit-breaker. We'll also surface enforcement decisions to Sentry/logs for enterprise customers.
QuotaBot: "enforcement.rule.created" event: plan=pro, rule_id=pr-203, burst=50000, window=60s
Ben: Metrics/dashboarding: make a dedicated "Quota" dashboard with widgets: current usage (per-plan), burst_consumption heatmap, top offenders (keys/orgs), recent throttle events. Expose it in the Console under Billing -> Quotas.
Priya: One more thing: cooldown policy after a hard deny — recommend exponential backoff on the client side and a 5m soft cooldown for free accounts, 1m for pro, 0 for enterprise (subject to support).
Alex: We should also create a short RFC doc and a tiny JSON schema for the enforcement config. I'll draft RFC and attach to the thread.
Maya: I can prototype the SDK header changes and a console mock.
Ben: I'll wire the dashboard panels and telemetry. ops-sre, can you own the proxy admission design?
ops-sre: Yep, will post a follow-up design later today.
Alex: Cool — action items: Priya draft RFC + schema, Ben dashboard, Maya SDK & console mock, ops-sre proxy design. We'll review in next eng-platform sync. :thumbsup:
Priya: Drafted RFC link (internal): https://redwood-internal/notes/quota-tier-proposal (mock)
Maya: adding a small example curl response for the API when throttled: ```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  # Response 429 
  # {"error":"quota_exceeded","quota_remaining":0,"burst_available":0,"reset_in":120}
```
Alex: thanks all, this is actionable. I'll collect the artifacts and close the loop.
